fields.quoted_span: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey.
fields.note: Most elements are supported (90-day notice, lease running longer, English/Spanish notice within 10 business days, posting for more than 10 units, court-rule notice, separate notice for monetary offers, five-day review, pressure tactics). But the guide says the 90-day notice applies when the buyer wants to personally occupy it as a primary residence, and that a tenant with a longer lease cannot be evicted until it expires; the rule's phrasing is consistent. The rule says the tenant notice tells them they 'need not move', which matches. Minor issue: the rule says 'harassment and rent increases above rent control or unconscionable increases', while the guide says 'unreasonable or unconscionable'. Overall mostly supported with slight paraphrase drift.

fields.quoted_span: must provide notices to the tenants in English and Spanish, within 10 business days after the sale
fields.note: The 90-day notice to quit for buyer occupancy, the 10-business-day tenant notice in English and Spanish, and the five-day review period are all stated in the guide.
The rule's effective_date is empty and the guide states no effective date for these foreclosure provisions.

fields.quoted_span: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey.
fields.note: The guide presents the protections as current law with no sign of repeal or suspension, so in_force is consistent.

fields.quoted_span: Any person acquiring a foreclosed property containing one or more residential rental units
fields.note: Min_units 1 and the owner-occupied two- and three-family point are supported by 'Month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units are not exempt from the 90-day notice requirements.' The trigger conditions match the document.

The guide cites N.J.S.A. 2A:50-69 et seq., 2A:50-70(c)2 for posting and 2A:50-71(b) for pressure tactics, so 2A:50-70 is supported only for the posting duty. The 90-day notice is grounded in Chase Manhattan Bank v. Josephson, not in the cited statute, as the review note itself acknowledges.
